About Banking On Quantum

Banking On Quantum is an international research and advisory initiative dedicated to preparing global financial infrastructure for the quantum era.

Strategic Objectives

  1. Protect Global Value: Eliminate vulnerability to Shor's algorithm by accelerating post-quantum cryptographic transitions across banks, payment networks, and sovereign wealth funds.
  2. Democratize Quantum Finance: Provide platform-agnostic algorithmic toolkits that enable financial analysts to execute quantum algorithms on diverse QPU hardware.
  3. Regulatory Guidance: Collaborate with central banks, the BIS Innovation Hub, and international standard-setting bodies to establish pragmatic quantum security mandates.

entries.title: Frequently Asked Questions | Banking On Quantum
entries.content:
Skip to main content Frequently Asked Questions | Banking On Quantum Authoritative answers to common questions regarding Banking On Quantum platform architecture, regulatory compliance, and implementation.

Questions? Answers.

Do quantum computers pose an immediate threat to financial encryption?

Yes. Although cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs) capable of breaking 2048-bit RSA and ECC are estimated to arrive within the next 5 to 8 years, adversarial entities are actively harvesting encrypted banking communications, ledger payloads, and wire transmissions today. Transitioning to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is required immediately to prevent retroactive decryption.

What is the "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" (HNDL) attack vector?

In a Harvest Now, Decrypt Later attack, state actors and cybercriminals record and store ciphertext passing through global financial networks. Even though they cannot decrypt it today with classical computers, the data will be completely decipherable once a quantum computer executes Shor's algorithm. For financial contracts, trade secrets, and sovereign identities with long confidentiality lifespans (10–30 years), the risk is present right now.

How does Post-Quantum Cryptography differ from Quantum Key Distribution?

Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is mathematical encryption that runs on standard classical servers, cloud environments, and existing internet protocols, relying on hard problems like lattice math that quantum computers cannot solve. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is physical-layer security using photons over dedicated dark-fibre lines to detect eavesdropping. PQC is deployable globally on existing infrastructure, whereas QKD provides physical-layer assurance between core inter-bank data centres.

What are the primary NIST-standardized algorithms adopted in banking?

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) finalized the primary post-quantum standards in 2024: FIPS 203 (ML-KEM) for key encapsulation and session establishment, FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) for primary digital signatures, and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA) for stateless hash-based backup signatures. Banking On Quantum integrates these standards into existing TLS 1.3 and HSM pipelines.

What is the global regulatory timeline for mandatory PQC migration?

Financial regulators including the US Federal Reserve, European Banking Authority (EBA), Bank of England (BoE), and Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) have mandated cryptographic discovery and migration roadmaps beginning in 2025. Full deprecation of legacy RSA and ECC keys in core payment rails and SWIFT messaging is targeted

entries.title: The Future of Banking and Finance | Banking On Quantum
entries.content:
Skip to main content The Future of Banking and Finance | Banking On QuantumPrepare financial institutions for the post-quantum era with Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), and quantum algorithms.

The Quantum Revolution in Financial Services

Quantum computing represents a paradigm shift for global banking infrastructure. From high-dimensional risk modeling and sub-millisecond derivative pricing to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), quantum technology is rewriting the rules of computational finance.

Core Strategic Focus Areas

1. Post-Quantum Cryptographic Migration (PQC)

With NIST finalizing post-quantum standards (FIPS 203 ML-KEM, FIPS 204 ML-DSA, FIPS 205 SLH-DSA), financial institutions face an urgent requirement to transition payment rails, core banking ledgers, and SWIFT messaging from vulnerable RSA/ECC algorithms to quantum-resistant standards.

2. Quantum Monte Carlo & Derivative Pricing

Quantum amplitude estimation delivers quadratic speedups over classical Monte Carlo methods, enabling real-time valuation of exotic derivatives, multi-asset risk simulations, and stress testing under volatile market conditions.

3. Combinatorial Portfolio & Liquidity Optimization

Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithms (QAOA) and quantum annealers solve complex NP-hard liquidity balancing, dynamic asset allocation, and cross-border settlement routing at scale.

4. Quantum-Safe Communications & QKD

Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) leverages the fundamental laws of physics to guarantee tamper-evident cryptographic key exchange across inter-bank data center backbones.

entries.title: Quantum Architecture & Cryptographic Agility | Banking On Quantum
entries.content:
Skip to main content Quantum Architecture & Cryptographic Agility | Banking On Quantum Architectural blueprint for post-quantum cryptographic migration, quantum algorithm integration, and hybrid quantum-classical computing.

Quantum Platform Architecture

Banking On Quantum establishes a vendor-agnostic, cryptographically agile framework that integrates hybrid classical-quantum computing into existing banking cores.

Core Architectural Layers

1. Cryptographic Agility & Key Management

  • NIST Post-Quantum Standards: Native support for ML-KEM (Kyber) for key encapsulation, ML-DSA (Dilithium) for digital signatures, and SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+) for stateless hash-based signing.
  • Hybrid TLS & Dual-Certificates: Concurrent validation of classical RSA/ECDSA and post-quantum keys ensuring zero downtime during multi-year institutional migration.

2. Quantum Algorithm Acceleration Engine

  • Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE): Quadratic speedups for Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall (ES) calculations.
  • QAOA & VQE Solvers: Optimal collateral allocation, cash-sweep optimization, and trade-clearing batch schedules.

3. Hardware-Agnostic Abstraction Layer

  • QPU Interoperability: Seamless execution across superconducting qubits, trapped-ion processors, photonic quantum hardware, and classical quantum simulators.

Quantum Solutions by Financial Sector

Explore high-impact applications of quantum technology across banking divisions.

  • PQC Migration Roadmap: Inventorying and upgrading all public-key infrastructure across hardware security modules (HSMs), core ledgers, and API gateways.
  • Harvest Now, Decrypt Later Defense: Immediate protection of encrypted wire transcripts and regulatory archives against adversary interception.

2. Capital Markets & Structured Products

  • Real-Time Risk Simulation: Calculating complex Greek sensitivities on multi-asset derivative books in seconds rather than overnight batch runs.
  • Algorithmic Arbitrage: Rapid identification of multi-leg arbitrage and market-making spreads across fragmented liquidity pools.

3. Corporate Treasury & Global Cash Management
